cohort: 100 women diagnosed with preeclampsia admitted to Patna Medical College and Hospital between October 2021 and October 2024.
finding: Combination therapy with antihypertensive drugs and magnesium sulfate was found most effective for maternal blood pressure control and complication reduction, though early planned delivery improved maternal outcomes at the cost of increased neonatal prematurity and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were more common among severe cases of preeclampsia when urgent delivery was indicated.
